clue.text: American expert is ready for action

parts.note: someone able is skilled or expert

explanation.surface: An American specialist stands prepared to get to work.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fit to be put into service straight away is serviceable, prepared for use.

clue.text: Is icy tomb built for everyone's benefit?

indicators.note: something built is assembled from its parts, so these letters are put together afresh

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a frozen tomb was constructed for the common good.
explanation.definitionFit: A mutually beneficial relationship between partners helps all parties involved.

clue.text: Gambled on stealing contents of cash cow?

indicators.note: the wager takes the cash's inside letters into itself

parts.note: to bet is to gamble, and bet is also the past tense

indicators.note: the contents of a word are its inside letters, without the ends

explanation.surface: Someone put money on a cash cow and dipped into the takings.
explanation.walkthrough: A cow is an example of the answer, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A cow is a farm animal, and farmers call cattle by this name.

clue.text: Censor piece probing former virgin?

parts.note: ex means former

indicators.note: the gun probes into the word for virgin

parts.note: virgin means pure, untouched
piece and gat are both slang for a gun

explanation.surface: A censor cuts a passage dealing with a former virgin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'piece' looks like a bit of text, but it is gun slang.
explanation.definitionFit: To remove objectionable parts from a text is to censor it.

clue.text: Transfer unit back

definitions.meaning: to move a staff member temporarily to another post or department
a basic measure of time, one sixtieth of a minute
to support a motion or proposal formally at a meeting

explanation.surface: Three unconnected words that read like a terse order to move a squad to the rear.
explanation.walkthrough: A triple definition: three separate senses of the one word, with no wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Staff can be lent to another department, time is measured in sixtieths of a minute, and a seconder supports a motion.

clue.text: Lecture promoted outside college

indicators.note: the word for promoted sits outside the college letter

parts.note: goods promoted by a salesperson are sold

explanation.surface: A lecturer was moved up to a post off campus.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'promoted' tempts a reversal; here it is simply a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: To tell someone off at length is to give them a talking-to.

clue.text: Unorthodox cleric had way of coping with issue

indicators.note: unorthodox means departing from the usual order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A maverick clergyman had a method for tackling a problem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'issue' reads as a problem, but in its sense of offspring it means children.
explanation.definitionFit: Issue means offspring, so looking after the young is how parents manage their kids.

clue.text: Diana represented female spirit

indicators.note: re-presented, these letters are presented again in another order

explanation.surface: The goddess Diana stood for a female spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth a water nymph is a female spirit of rivers and springs.

clue.text: Line feeding father's mother vital fluid

indicators.note: the line letter feeds into the family words

parts.note: pa is father, so pa's is father's
ma is mother

explanation.surface: A tube supplies the paternal grandmother with a life-sustaining liquid.
explanation.definitionFit: The liquid part of blood, carrying cells round the body, is a fluid essential to life.

clue.text: Corresponded about grey seals

indicators.note: the word for grey seals the word for about inside it

parts.note: grey-haired, hence aged
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: Someone wrote letters about grey seals, the marine mammals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grey seals' reads as the animal; 'seals' is the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that tally or match correspond, as accounts that are consistent.

clue.text: Start to like novel proposition

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, so only the first letter of like is used

parts.note: Emma is the novel by Jane Austen

explanation.surface: A reader is beginning to enjoy a fresh idea put to them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like an adjective meaning new, but it names the book.
explanation.definitionFit: In mathematics a subsidiary theorem proved on the way to a larger result is a proposition of this kind.

clue.text: Vocalist's autobiographical sketch after concert's likely to be good

indicators.note: the singer's self-description comes after the concert in the answer

parts.note: a prom is a promenade concert, such as the BBC Proms; the 's stands for 'is', linking to the definition
a singer describing themselves in two words would say 'I sing'

explanation.surface: A singer's account of their own life, following a concert, suggests a bright future.
explanation.walkthrough: The Proms are a famous summer series of classical concerts in London; 'I sing' is the vocalist's whole life story in miniature.
explanation.definitionFit: Showing signs of future success means something is expected to turn out well.

clue.text: Equipment in desert manoeuvres moved quickly

indicators.note: the equipment sits inside the rearranged letters
letters put through manoeuvres are shifted about into a new order

parts.note: kit is gear or equipment

explanation.surface: Kit used in army exercises in the desert was shifted at speed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'desert manoeuvres' reads as army exercises, but 'manoeuvres' is the anagram signal, giving STERED, and 'in' places the equipment after its S.
explanation.definitionFit: To scamper with light, fast movements, as a small animal does, is to move hurriedly.

clue.text: Electric car avoids M20

indicators.note: the car steers clear of the letter M, so that letter is dropped

parts.note: a dodgem is an electrically powered bumper car at a fairground

explanation.surface: An electric vehicle steers clear of the M20 motorway in Kent.
explanation.walkthrough: M20 is not a road at all: the M is the letter to remove and 20 points to the answer at 20 across, which is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer to 20 across means to avoid, and to sidestep something is exactly that.

clue.text: Father's not taking part in mad prank

indicators.note: the priest's abbreviation stays out of the word for mad, so those letters are removed

parts.note: frantic means wild, mad with worry
Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest's title; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: A priest declines to join in a crazy practical joke.
explanation.definitionFit: A playful, absurd caper or trick is a piece of buffoonery of this sort.

clue.text: Met new limit introduced by company director

indicators.note: the new limit is brought in between the company and director letters

parts.note: a verge is an edge or limit

explanation.surface: A company director brought in a fresh cap and met with approval.
explanation.definitionFit: Lines or people coming together at one point have joined up.

clue.text: Appealed to court about leaflet putting Democrat last

indicators.note: putting the party's letter somewhere new moves it within the word
the party's letter is taken to the very end
the word for court goes around the word for leaflet

parts.note: to court someone is to date them
a tract is a pamphlet or leaflet
D is the abbreviation for Democrat in US politics

explanation.surface: A litigant took their case to a court over a pamphlet that ranked the Democrat at the bottom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'court' looks legal but means woo. 'about' gives DATTRACTE, and 'putting Democrat last' sends that D to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that drew people in or held their interest was alluring to them.

clue.text: Cut back duty originally capped by fuel regulator

indicators.note: in a down entry, the duty letter has the regulator on top of it

parts.note: a throttle controls the flow of fuel to an engine

indicators.note: originally means the word duty supplies only its opening letter

explanation.surface: A fuel regulator cut back the duty, at first held down by a cap.
explanation.definitionFit: To be restricted or choked off, as output or speed is reduced, is to be curtailed.

clue.text: Announcement of resignation disrupted late shift

indicators.note: letters disrupted are thrown out of order and rearranged

explanation.surface: A worker announces they are quitting after a late shift is upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resignation' looks like quitting a job, but here it is resigned acceptance.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrug at misfortune is the phrase that expresses resigned acceptance of how things are.

clue.text: Someone who relates swimming race to run

indicators.note: letters swimming about are in motion and land in a new order

explanation.surface: A swimmer is moving from one event, a swimming race, to a run, as in a triathlon.
explanation.definitionFit: A skilled teller of anecdotes is a person who narrates stories.

clue.text: After losing cases Iron Maiden drops one crew member

indicators.note: in a down entry the numeral drops one place lower in the word
losing cases strips each word of its outer letters, leaving only the insides

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Heavy metal band Iron Maiden sack a roadie after losing court cases.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing cases' gives RO and AIDE; then 'drops' lowers the I one place in the down entry, turning ROAIDE into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A touring band's road crew includes the person who sets up and moves the gear.

clue.text: Avoid woman who was tempted to grab publicity

indicators.note: the tempted woman grabs and holds the publicity inside her

parts.note: Eve was tempted by the serpent in Genesis
an ad is an advertisement, a piece of publicity

explanation.surface: Keep away from the woman who was tempted to seek fame.
explanation.walkthrough: A nod to the setter, Serpent, who did the tempting.
explanation.definitionFit: To dodge or escape something is to keep clear of it.

clue.text: Keepers at zoo looking after cod

indicators.note: keepers looking after something hold it, so the answer is held within these words

explanation.surface: Zookeepers are caring for a fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cod' looks like the fish, but as an adjective it means mock or sham.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective, cod means fake or imitation, as in a cod accent.

clue.text: Walk before 12 ran briefly

parts.note: a.m., ante meridiem, is the time before twelve noon

indicators.note: cut short, so the word for ran loses its final letter

parts.note: dye or colour that ran has bled

explanation.surface: A walk is followed by a hasty dash before noon.
explanation.definitionFit: A leisurely stroll is an unhurried kind of walk.

clue.text: Lovely rose without red exterior

indicators.note: without means lacking, so these letters are taken away
the letters go from the outside, the front and the back

parts.note: rose up in revolt, so rebelled

explanation.surface: A beautiful rose lacking the usual red outer petals.
explanation.walkthrough: RE comes off the front and D off the back, the letters of 'red' round the outside.
explanation.definitionFit: A lovely, as a noun, is a beautiful woman, a beauty of the ball.

clue.text: Purification of medieval Christians' lives

parts.note: the Cathars were a dualist Christian sect of medieval southern France
lives means exists, is

explanation.surface: A study of how a medieval sect lived as a cleansing exercise.
explanation.definitionFit: Emotional release or cleansing, from the Greek for purging, is a kind of purification.

clue.text: Secretly deposit funds in reporter's account

indicators.note: a reporter's account is spoken, so the word is as heard

parts.note: funds are money, cash

explanation.surface: Funds are hidden away in a journalist's bank account.
explanation.definitionFit: To stash something in a hidden store is to hide it for later use.

clue.text: Check credit rating that's out of place

indicators.note: the place abbreviation is taken out of the word

parts.note: a plaudit gives someone credit, cryptically a rating of their credit
Pl is the abbreviation for place, as in street addresses

explanation.surface: Verify a credit score that seems wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'credit rating' looks financial but means praise; 'that's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An official inspection of accounts is an examination or verification.

clue.text: I left soldier in pub without any reason

indicators.note: the soldier goes in the pub

parts.note: a local is the pub nearest one's home
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: Someone recalls walking out on a soldier in a bar for no good reason.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking sense or logic is acting with no rational basis.

clue.text: Meaning of two papers written by doctor

indicators.note: the papers follow the doctor, as if written after his name

parts.note: the i and the FT (Financial Times) are two British newspapers

explanation.surface: The sense of a pair of articles a doctor has authored.
explanation.walkthrough: The i is a British daily newspaper, and the FT is the Financial Times.
explanation.definitionFit: The general gist or import of what someone says is its sense.

clue.text: Interfere with gong's sound

indicators.note: the sound of the word for gong is what the answer echoes

parts.note: gong is British slang for a medal or decoration

explanation.surface: Someone tampers with the noise a gong makes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gong' looks like the percussion instrument, but here it is slang for an award.
explanation.definitionFit: To poke into affairs that are not one's own is to intrude.

clue.text: Show Havering and Barking tried closing hospital

definitions.note: havering is dithering, so to show havering is to dither, a verb

indicators.note: the rearranged letters close round the hospital letter
barking means mad, so the letters go crazy into a new order

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: Havering and Barking, two London boroughs, tried shutting a hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: Havering and Barking look like neighbouring London boroughs (Barking and Dagenham is one); here 'havering' means hesitating and 'Barking' means mad. 'Barking' turns TRIED into DITER, and 'closing' puts H inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To hesitate indecisively is to waver, which is what havering means.
